WITH MonthlyRevenue AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id, 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, 
        SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS revenue
    FROM 
        public.orders o
    JOIN 
        public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    GROUP BY 
        o.customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)
),
FirstLastMonthRevenue AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        MIN(month) AS first_month,
        MAX(month) AS last_month
    FROM 
        MonthlyRevenue
    GROUP BY 
        customer_id
),
CustomerGrowth AS (
    SELECT 
        mr.customer_id,
        flmr.first_month,
        flmr.last_month,
        SUM(CASE WHEN mr.month = flmr.first_month THEN mr.revenue ELSE 0 END) AS first_month_revenue,
        SUM(CASE WHEN mr.month = flmr.last_month THEN mr.revenue ELSE 0 END) AS last_month_revenue
    FROM 
        MonthlyRevenue mr
    JOIN 
        FirstLastMonthRevenue flmr ON mr.customer_id = flmr.customer_id
    GROUP BY 
        mr.customer_id, flmr.first_month, flmr.last_month
    HAVING 
        COUNT(DISTINCT mr.month) >= 5
)
SELECT 
    cg.customer_id, 
    cu.company_name, 
    cg.first_month_revenue, 
    cg.last_month_revenue, 
    (cg.last_month_revenue - cg.first_month_revenue) AS revenue_growth
FROM 
    CustomerGrowth cg
JOIN 
    public.customers cu ON cg.customer_id = cu.customer_id
ORDER BY 
    revenue_growth DESC
LIMIT 10;

HX2.question: Welche Regionen erzielen hohen Umsatz, obwohl ihre Auftragszahl unter dem Median liegt?
HX2.final_response_text: Es gibt keine Regionen, die einen hohen Umsatz erzielen, obwohl ihre Auftragszahl unter dem Median liegt. Alle Regionen mit einem Umsatz über dem Median haben auch eine entsprechende Anzahl an Aufträgen. Wenn du weitere Analysen benötigst, lass es mich wissen!
HX2.sql_query:
WITH RegionUmsatz AS (
    SELECT 
        r.region_description, 
        SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM public.region r
    JOIN public.territories t ON r.region_id = t.region_id
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.ship_region = r.region_description
    JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    GROUP BY r.region_description
),
MedianOrderCount AS (
    SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY order_count) AS median_order_count
    FROM RegionUmsatz
)
SELECT 
    region_description, 
    total_revenue, 
    order_count
FROM RegionUmsatz, MedianOrderCount
WHERE order_count < median_order_count
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

HX9.sql_query:
SELECT s.company_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS product_count, 
       SUM(od.quantity) AS total_sold, 
       CASE WHEN COUNT(p.product_id) > 0 THEN SUM(od.quantity) * 1.0 / COUNT(p.product_id) ELSE 0 END AS sold_ratio
FROM public.suppliers s
JOIN public.products p ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
LEFT JOIN public.order_details od ON p.product_id = od.product_id
GROUP BY s.company_name
HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) > 5 AND (SUM(od.quantity) * 1.0 / COUNT(p.product_id)) < 1
ORDER BY sold_ratio ASC, product_count DESC

       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) AS Gesamtumsatz, 
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS Bestellungen_pro_Kunde
FROM public.customer_customer_demo ccd

JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

HX13.question: Welche Mitarbeitenden dominieren einzelne Regionen stark (Anteil groesser als 50 Prozent des Regionalumsatzes)?
HX13.final_response_text: Es gibt derzeit keine Mitarbeitenden, die mehr als 50% des Umsatzes in einer einzelnen Region dominieren. Wenn du weitere Analysen benötigst oder die Kriterien anpassen möchtest, lass es mich wissen!
HX13.sql_query:
WITH regional_totals AS (
    SELECT t.region_id, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) AS total_sales
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    JOIN public.territories t ON o.ship_region = t.territory_id
    GROUP BY t.region_id
)
SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, r.region_description, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) AS regional_sales
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
JOIN public.employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN public.territories t ON o.ship_region = t.territory_id
JOIN public.region r ON t.region_id = r.region_id
JOIN regional_totals rt ON t.region_id = rt.region_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, r.region_description, rt.total_sales
HAVING SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) > 0.5 * rt.total_sales
ORDER BY regional_sales DESC;

HX14.sql_query:
WITH AverageBasketValue AS (
    SELECT customer_id, AVG(total_value) AS avg_basket_value
    FROM (
        SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_value
        FROM public.orders o
        JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
        GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id
    ) AS order_totals
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
ProductFamilyCount AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) AS product_family_count
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON od.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY o.customer_id
),
OverallAverage AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_basket_value) AS overall_avg
    FROM AverageBasketValue
)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, abv.avg_basket_value, pfc.product_family_count
FROM public.customers c
JOIN AverageBasketValue abv ON c.customer_id = abv.customer_id
JOIN ProductFamilyCount pfc ON c.customer_id = pfc.customer_id
JOIN OverallAverage oa ON abv.avg_basket_value < oa.overall_avg
WHERE pfc.product_family_count > 1
ORDER BY abv.avg_basket_value ASC, pfc.product_family_count DESC
LIMIT 10;
